messages:
ana_marketing: Hey team — prepping the webinar narrative and we want a small, high-signal benchmark package that illustrates warmup vs steady-state tradeoffs. Can runtime own a narrow-slice deliverable for marketing?

ana_marketing: Ask is: compact, reproducible artifacts we can show in slides + appendix. Not asking for a full sweep — just a focused set we can trust.

ana_marketing: Requested outputs (ideal):
- a seed set of 25 representative prompts (short/med/long split)
- 3 model variants: FP16 baseline, int8 quantized, int4 quantized (if supported)
- coldstart heatmap: first-token latency distribution across ~1000 cold runs
- steady-state throughput profile: p50/p90/p99 token latency and token/sec at a couple of concurrency points
- top 5 outlier traces and 10 raw sample outputs (for quality sanity check)
- a tiny repro snippet (curl or SDK) and the warmup command used

ana_marketing: Timeline: need everything by EOD next Tue if possible (to lock slides). If that's unrealistic, call it out and tell me the minimal viable subset.

mike_runtime: Got it — we can do a narrow slice. A couple of quick q's: do you want per-model-per-variant breakdown (i.e., separate tables for each quantization), or a combined view with deltas? Also are synthetic payloads OK or do you need production-derived examples?

ana_marketing: Per-model-per-variant please — we want to call out the delta between baseline and quantized. Production-derived examples preferred for the sample outputs, but we can redact. Synthetic is fine for the heatmaps if getting production examples will delay things.

mike_runtime: Cool. Note: int4 may not be available for every model; we'll report availability and fallback behavior. Running the coldstart heatmap across 1000 runs per cell will take some compute; I can do a constrained run (500) if we need to save credit/time. Which would you prefer?

ana_marketing: If you can do 1000 for short and med prompts and 500 for long that sounds fine. prioritize short/med.

sam_sre: Heads-up: include the runtime tags and quant profile names in the artifacts (e.g., q8_00, q4_v2, fp16). Also capture instance type and kernel build id so marketing can attach a reproducibility note.

mike_runtime: Will do. We'll include a small metadata.json per run with the tags you mentioned. Quick repro snippet we'll include:

mike_runtime: ```bash
# warmup + single request example
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" 
  -d '{"model":"model-name","input":"<prompt>","max_tokens":128}'
```

mike_runtime: For the coldstart heatmap we use a fresh process per run to simulate real coldstarts — that's what marketing usually expects. Confirm?

ana_marketing: Yes, fresh process per run please. Also include a tiny doc blurb we can copy into slides: 2-3 bullets explaining methodology + caveats (warmup behavior, variability, how we measured).

devon_runtime: I'll own the run and upload artifacts to the marketing bucket. Plan: start tonight, run small smoke tomorrow, full sweep Mon-Tue. If we hit regen issues we'll flip to the 500-run long prompt plan.

ana_marketing: Amazing — please @mike_runtime and @devon_runtime in the final drop. Also, can you surface the 5 sample outputs with short annotations if any generation looks degraded in quantized variants? even 1-line notes is fine.

mike_runtime: Yep — we'll flag any quality regressions and attach the raw outputs + a short note.

ci-bot: deploy:bench-slice job queued by devon_runtime (job id: 849210) :white_check_mark:

devon_runtime: Putting an initial checklist here for transparency: 1) confirm model list (which 3?) 2) get 25 prompt seed from marketing 3) run smoke 4) full runs 5) export artifacts + metadata

ana_marketing: Model list suggestion: redwood-v1-medium (fp16), redwood-v1-medium-q8 (int8), redwood-v1-medium-q4 (int4) — adjust if names differ. Sending seed prompts now in a follow-up DM.

mike_runtime: Sounds good. I'll update this thread when smoke completes with ETA for the full artifacts (likely Tue morning PST).
